abilities.name: Darkvision 60' (+30')
abilities.description: Your cursed anatomy grants you superior vision in dark and dim conditions. You can see in dim light within 60 feet of you as if it were bright light, and in darkness as if it were dim light. You can’t discern color in darkness, only shades of gray.

abilities.name: Blood Feasting
abilities.description: on a short rest I can drink the blood from a corpse and regain proficiency bonus worth of hit dice. Can only gain max level woth of hit dice per long rest.

abilities.description: I'm under the effects of hte spider climb spell at all times. Cannon be detected not dispelled except by Wish level magic.

I cannot be disarmed from my weapon bond unless incapacitated

With a Bonus Action I can teleport my weapon bond to me if it is on the same plane

I can have 2 weapon bonds

abilities.name: Maneuver Specialist
abilities.description:
Choose a maneuver to spcialize in. you can:
increase your DC +1
decrease exertion cost 1
increase damage +2

abilities.name: Blessing of Boreas: Cold Aegis
abilities.description: If you take Cold damage, you can use your Reaction to give yourself Resistance to Cold damage until the end of your next turn. You can use this Reaction a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

abilities.name: Blessing of Boreas: Winter Magic
abilities.description: You know the Ray of Frost cantrip. Choose either the Armor of Agathys or Ice Knife spell. You always have that spell prepared. You can cast the spell once without a spell slot, and you regain the ability to cast it in that way when you finish a Long Rest. You can also cast this spell using any spell slots you have. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for this feat’s spells (choose when you select this feat).

abilities.name: Darkwood Magic
abilities.description: You know the pestilence cantrip. At 3rd level, you can cast either fog cloud or inflict wounds once between long rests. At 5th level, you can cast either acid arrow or invisibility once between long rests. Your spellcasting ability for these is your choice of Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma.

abilities.name: Walking Corpse
abilities.description: Your creature type is both Humanoid and Undead. You do not need to breathe. When a creature would deal you necrotic damage, at their option they can heal you for that amount instead. Once you have been healed this way, you can’t be again until you finish a long rest.

abilities.name: Already Dead
abilities.description: You are immune to disease. You have resistance to poison damage, and advantage on saving throws against the poisoned condition.

abilities.name: Fanged Bite
abilities.description:
The bite is a natural weapon, which you can use to make unarmed strikes that deal equal to 1d4 piercing damage. Attack and damage rolls with your bite use your choice of Strength, Dexterity, or Constitution modifiers.

While you or your target are bloodied, you gain an expertise die on these attack rolls.

abilities.name: Reserves
abilities.description: At 4th level your stamina increases, allowing you to engage foes longer without tiring. Your exertion pool increases by 1. At 8th, 12th, and 16th level your exertion pool increases by an additional point.

abilities.name: Newblood
abilities.description:
You have been corrupted with vampirism from exposure to dark forces that unlocked an ancient and unknown power within your blood, or because a vampire has bitten you. In either case your affliction makes you more than mortal, and yet somehow less.

You gain resistance to necrotic damage (or if you already have it, immunity to necrotic damage) and darkvision to a range of 30 feet (or if you already have it, the range of your darkvision increases by 30 feet). You also gain a bite natural weapon and the Charming Gaze feature.

Bite. You gain a bite natural weapon you are proficient with. You are only able to bite grappled , incapacitated , restrained , or willing creatures. On a hit your bite deals piercing damage equal to 1d6 plus your Strength modifier or Dexterity modifier (whichever is highest). You can use Dexterity instead of Strength for the attack rolls of your bite. In addition, once per turn you can choose for your bite to also deal 1d6 necrotic damage × your proficiency bonus. You regain hit points equal to the amount of necrotic damage dealt to your target. This necrotic damage can only be increased by a critical hit. 

Charming Gaze. You magically target a creature within 30 feet, forcing it to make a Wisdom saving throw (DC 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Charisma modifier). On a failure, the target is charmed by you for a number of hours equal to your proficiency bonus. While charmed it regards you as a trusted friend and is a willing target for your bite. The target repeats the saving throw each time it takes damage, ending the effect on itself on a success. If the target’s saving throw is successful or the effect ends for it, it is immune to your charm for 24 hours. Once you have used this feature, you can’t do so again until you finish a long rest.

This dark gift comes with a price however, making you averse to sunlight. You have disadvantage on attack rolls and on Perception checks that rely on sight when you, the target of your attack, or whatever you are trying to perceive is in direct sunlight. In addition, you cannot use your Charming Gaze while you are in direct sunlight.

combat_maneuvers.name: Mystic Feint
combat_maneuvers.description: When a creature makes a melee attack roll against you, you can use your reaction to gain an expertise die to your AC against that creature. This increase only applies to the attacking creature and ends at the start of your next turn. Once the attack is resolved, you may choose to switch spaces with the target. This movement does not provoke opportunity attacks .

spells.name: Pestilence
spells.description:
A swarm of insects fills the area. Creatures that begin their turn within the spell’s area or who enter the area for the first time on their turn must make a Constitution saving throw or take 1d4 piercing damage. The pests also ravage any unattended organic material within their radius, such as plant, wood, or fabric.

This spell’s damage increases by 1d4 when you reach 5th level (2d4), 10th level (3d4), and 15th level (4d4).

spells.name: Hoarfrost
spells.description:
Evocation Cantrip

A melee Weapon you are holding is imbuded with cold. For teh duration, a rime of frost covers the weapon and light vapor rises from it if the teperature is above freezing.  The weapon beomes magical and deals an extra 1d4 cold damageon a successful hit. The spesll ends after 1 minute, or earlier if you make a successful attack or let go of it.

The spell damage increases by 1d4 when you reach 5th level (2d4), 11th level (3d4), and 17th level (4d4).

Deep Magic Volume 1 page 210

spells.name: Prestidigitation
spells.description:
You wield arcane energies to produce minor effects. Choose one of the following: 

* create a single burst of magic that manifests to one of the senses (for example a burst of sound, sparks, or an odd odor).
* clean or soil an object of 1 cubic foot or less.
* light or snuff a flame.
* chill, warm, or flavor nonliving material of 1 cubic foot or less for 1 hour.
* color or mark an object or surface for 1 hour.
* create an ordinary trinket or illusionary image that fits in your hand and lasts for 1 round.

You may cast this spell multiple times, though only three effects may be active at a time. Dismissing each effect requires an action.

spells.name: Fog Cloud
spells.description:
You create a heavily obscured area of fog. The fog spreads around corners and can be dispersed by a moderate wind (at least 10 miles per hour).

Cast at Higher Levels
The spell’s radius increases by 20 feet for each slot level above 1st.

spells.name: Inflict Wounds
spells.description:
You impart fell energies that suck away the target’s life force, making a melee spell attack that deals 3d10 necrotic damage.

Cast at Higher Levels
The damage increases by 1d10 for each slot level above 1st.

spells.name: Shadow Armor
spells.description:
1st Level Abjuration
Trigger: When targeted by an attack, but before the the roll is made.

You can siphon energy from the Plane of Shadow to protect yourself from an immediate threat. As a reaction, you pull shadows around yourself to distort reality. The attack against you is made with disadvantage, and you have resistance to radiant damage until yhe start of your next turn.

Deep MAgic Volume 2 Page 216

spells.name: Elemental Rebound
spells.description:
You redirect and reflect a portion of incoming elemental energy. You gain resistance to the damage type that triggered this spell, which applies against the incoming damage. The next time you deal damage before this spell ends, one of your targets takes 1d6 damage of the triggering type. Dealing this extra damage ends the spell early.

MOAR 222

spells.name: Ice Bolts
spells.description:
You create three bolts of ice that you direct at one or more creatures within range and line of sight. Each bolt hits automatically and does 1d6 cold damage. The bolts all strike simultaneously.

Enhancement: For each spell slot used higher than 1st level, you create one additional bolt.

Book of Lost Spells 73

spells.name: Armor of Agathys
spells.description:
Protective magical frost surrounds you. You gain 5 Temporary Hit Points. If a creature hits you with a melee attack roll before the spell ends, the creature takes 5 Cold damage. The spell ends early if you have no Temporary Hit Points.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. The Temporary Hit Points and the Cold damage both increase by 5 for each spell slot level above 1.

spells.name: Ray of Frost
spells.description:
An icy beam shoots from your outstretched fingers. Make a ranged spell attack . On a hit, you deal 1d8 cold damage and reduce the target’s Speed by 10 feet until the start of your next turn.

This spell’s damage increases by 1d8 when you reach 5th level (2d8), 11th level (3d8), and 17th level (4d8).

spells.name: Calculated Retribution
spells.description:
1st-level (AbjurationForceLawWeaponry)
Components:VSM (executioner’s hood)

You surround yourself with a dampening magical field and collect the energy of a foe’s attack to use against them. When you take damage from a weapon attack, you can end the spell to halve the attack’s damage against you, gaining a retribution charge that lasts until the end of your next turn. By expending the retribution charge when you hit with a melee attack, you deal an additional 2d10 force damage.

Cast at Higher Levels
You may use your reaction to halve the damage of an attack against you up to a number of times equal to the level of the spell slot used, gaining a retribution charge each time that lasts until 1 round after the spell ends. You must still make Constitution saving throws to maintain your concentration on this spell, but you do so with advantage , or if you already have advantage, you automatically succeed.

notes.title: Back Story
notes.body_md:
## 

## Torak's Sire: The General (Alaric). 

In life, the General fell to an onslaught of Chernobog's feral vampires (Draugr). They infected him with their curse, but his own burning will and hatred of the undead allowed him to choose his own fate. He spent decades upon decades recruiting the toughest warriors into service. Those who survived his training were given the chance to join the Einherjar.  He hand-picked Torak and, in a ritual out on the tundra and in the heart of a blizzard, drove a shard of starlight ice into the young soldier's chest, replacing his heart with the Frost of the North. 

When Hrimm-Kastel fell, Alaric stayed behind to buy time for the others to flee and brought many traitors down. Their bloody, dying screams followed Torak and his family as they fled to Ironcrag Hold. Torak dreams of his sire wandering the Bleak Expanse, a broken spear with an orange-glowing tip in his hand as he hunts the enemy. 

## The Widow's Nail

The fortress your family controlled along the wall is called Hrimm-Kastjel (Rime Bastion) by the dwarves, but it is also known as the "Widow's Nail" by the human and giant Jarls. It was a human, Jarl Hlothar Kurgensson, who led the betrayal. He was the leader of a settlement near the wall and provided your family with supplies. A rumour of an ancient artifact in the deep dungeons of the fortress caused him to betray you and your family to get at the relic. You never heard any such rumour. 

## The Dwarves

The survivors fled to Ironcrag Hold. The dwarves there, led by Thane Hreidmar "Stone-Eye," are Clan Bofyr. These dwarves referred to your family as "Einherjar," an important distinction. The north has many undead types, especially on the other side of the Wall, but most vampires are feral Darakhul, lowly beasts little better than ghouls. Einherjar are referred to as the Heroic Dead, who gave up Valhalla to continue the fight in the mortal world. 

Thane Stone-Eye, who has a carved sapphire in his left eye socket, is said to be able to see through half-truths and illusions. He is a devout follower of Wotan. 

One final secret: one of the ancestors of Clan Bofyr is a dwarven vampire wizard who was the one who recommended the thane ally with your people. You know of this secret, as it was part of why you trusted the thane. He gave you this secret to prove his loyalty and respect.

The clan is watched over by an Einjerjar, a 1500-year-old vampire named Valdrin Bofyr, Deep-Root of the Mountain, Master of the Old Oaths of Stone and Blood. Valdrin has given Torak a blood oath to protect the remaining members of his family. The elder vampire awoke from torpor when the fortress fell and Alaric was slain. His skin has taken a rough, stone-like texture, and when he slumbers most would mistake him for a statue of a dwarf on a throne in a forgotten chamber high on the mountain.
